data.one_liner: Flutter widget that wraps the native iOS UITextView and Android EditText for text input.
data.what_it_does: It provides a text field implemented with the platform's native controls, giving the same look, feel and behavior as the system widgets. The widget exposes common TextField properties and iOS‑specific options through a Flutter API.
use_when: You need native‑level text editing features such as precise cursor handling or custom font support on iOS/Android
Your app targets mobile only and wants the exact platform text‑input experience
You require Android support in addition to iOS for a unified native input widget
avoid_when: A simple cross‑platform TextField is sufficient and you don't need native fidelity
You target web or desktop platforms
You need extensive custom UI beyond what the native view offers
strengths: Native look and feel on iOS and Android
Supports custom font families and detailed iOS options
Handles cursor color, placeholder styling, and return key types
weaknesses: Only works on mobile platforms (no web/desktop)
Adds a native bridge which can increase app size and complexity
Limited to the features exposed by the plugin; deep customization may require platform code
